text:
arin: Heads-up — I’m seeing a noticeable spike in eval regressions after the q4b quant bring-up. Failing cohort looks like long prompt + code-completion tasks (ctx > 1024). Baseline -> quant-4bit avg pass rate down ~4.7% on the golden set. Posting quick harness diff and failing IDs below. :eyes:

ravi: Can you paste the harness output and a couple example failing prompt IDs?

arin: Sure — excerpt from the eval harness (trimmed):

```
# eval: quant-4b vs baseline
cohort: long-code-complete
baseline_pass: 0.912
quant4b_pass: 0.865
delta: -0.047
failing_examples: ["p_10324","p_32789","p_410221","p_410222"]
err_samples: {
  p_410221: {expected: "def foo():\n  return 42", model: "def foo() -> int: return42"},
  p_410222: {expected: "for i in range(5):\n  print(i)", model: "for i in range(5): print(i)"}
}
```

maya: Noted. That pattern (tight formatting diff in code outputs) smells like tokenizer or shortprefix KV cache mismatch we saw with tokenizer v2. Also possibility of near-duplicate prompts in the golden set confusing the pass metric. Could be dedupe collision.

lina: Labelers flagged several examples where the rubric was ambiguous for "format-preserving" outputs — they labeled them inconsistent. I'll paste one labeler note: "expected formatting required newline between def and return, model flattened to single line -> marked incorrect but borderline."

sam: Proposal: create a temporary "backstop" golden subset for the failing cohort (target N=500 high-agreement items) that blocks quant model rollouts until pass rate recovers. Steps: 1) sample targeted cohort, 2) dedupe + fingerprint check, 3) label with strict formatting rules, 4) add to CI/harness as hard gate. Timeline: 72 hours if we parallelize. Thoughts? :thumbsup:

maya: I can run the sampler and stratify by prompt length + task type. Will bias to examples where ctx > 1024 and code tokens > 30. Where should I output?

ravi: I'll run a dedupe pass and fingerprint regen. Using current tools: `scripts/fingerprint_regen.py --cohort long-code-complete --window=48h`. Will also run near-duplicate clustering (min-sim 0.92). Command I’ll run in 30m and post results.

ops-bot: Incident: quant-4b-deploy triggered canary alerts at 10:12 UTC — linked to failing cohort patterns. (automated)

arin: For the harness, I'll add a strict formatting-checker hook so we can separate semantic vs formatting errors. Patch will be small: add `format_strict=True` for code cohorts. PR when ready.

lina: I can spin up 2 labelers and put them on a high-precision queue for the next 48h. Need final sampling file + clear rubric with examples. I'll reuse the format-preserve checklist from the doc below: https://redwood.internal/docs/label-rubrics#format-preserve

maya: sampling plan: 600 candidates -> dedupe -> aim for ~500 after QC. Will output raw sample to `s3://redwood-curation/tmp/backstop_1768412345.jsonl`

ravi: dedupe run finished — quick summary (pasted):

```
input: 600 candidates
fingerprints before: 600
fingerprints unique after hash_v2: 584
near-dup clusters (min_sim 0.92): 18 clusters collapsed -> final 566
flagged possible collisions: [p_410221, p_410222]
```

maya: Pulling those flagged IDs out and adding manual inspection tag.

lina: Uploaded rubric + examples to the label queue. One question: do we accept single-line but semantically correct code? (that's currently the ambiguity). I recommend rule: preserve linebreaks if expected output includes them in golden; otherwise allow semantic-only.

sam: Agree on the rule. Add to the harness docs and make it explicit in the backstop gating criteria: 1) semantic correctness AND 2) formatting preserved when golden exhibits formatting.

arin: Opening PR for harness change now — https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4248 (WIP). It will add `format_strict` and annotate failing items with `format_violation` tag so we can track regressions separately.

maya: Starting manual pass on flagged collisions. ETA ~6 hours for first 100. Will post updates.

ravi: Dropping final dedupe + sample to s3: `s3://redwood-curation/backstop/1768412345_samples.jsonl` — permission = eng-ml-read.

lina: Labelers picked first batch (50). Early notes: 8/50 are borderline formatting-only. Marking those for arbitration.

sam: Good. Once we hit 500 agreed (>= 4/5 agreement), we add to CI as hard gate and re-run quant4b benchmark. If pass recovers to within 0.5% delta vs baseline on both semantic+format gate, we can greenlight a controlled canary.

arin: TL;DR action items: maya -> finish sampling + stratify; ravi -> final dedupe + upload; lina -> run label queue + arbitration; sam -> update gating doc + own rollout decision. Ops-bot will continue to monitor canary.

maya: On it. starting sample job now. :rocket:

ravi: Will post dedupe logs and cluster ids when done.

lina: Labelers queued, will triage arbitration after first 200.

sam: Thanks all — please ping me if you hit resource blockers.

arin: Filing follow-up thread if we need to debate rubric edgecases. For now, let's treat this as a backstop block for quant rollouts.

ops-bot: Scheduled reminder in 24h to check status of `backstop/1768412345`.
